title: Introduce prefill optimizer and quant prober CLI
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Customers need safer, automated defaults for prefill/batching/caching and conservative quantization recommendations that preserve unit economics while minimizing latency and token cost. This PR introduces a lightweight Prefill Optimizer CLI and an interactive Quant Prober that produce tenant-specific default profiles (batch shapes, cache TTLs, quant tiers) from sampled traces and synthetic probes.

What this change does: introduces a new CLI command (redwood econ prefill-scan) that ingests a small trace or runs a synthetic sampler against a tenant workload, runs a constrained search over batch/cache/quant configurations, and emits: 1) a ranked set of default profiles for tenant deployment, 2) deterministic cost/latency estimates, and 3) a dry-run policy that can be applied as a prefill-policy via the existing policy API. The Quant Prober runs in two modes: safe-probe (low Q aggression for production sampling) and fast-probe (higher aggression for lab sims).

Design notes: the optimizer uses a constrained hill-climb with simulated KV-cache and microbatch costs (cost model pluggable). The prober includes a small microbenchmark harness that executes model micro-batches with representative sequence lengths to measure token latency deltas for fp16/int8/4-bit-like runtimes. Outputs are compact JSON profiles plus an human-readable summary.

Checklist: 
- [x] CLI scaffolding and help text
- [x] Prefill optimizer kernel + cost model integration
- [x] Quant prober harness + safe-probe mode
- [x] Unit tests and integration test with synthetic traces
- [x] Telemetry events for generated profiles
- [x] Docs stub and example output included

Rollout plan: merged behind feature flag econ.prefill_optimizer; staged rollout 10% tenants for 48h, monitor unit_econ.delta and latency.p95; fallback path included in CLI to revert policy.

Follow-ups (future PRs): add auto-apply heuristics, tenant GQL export, and a lightweight UI in Console for profile diffs.

Notes: this is intentionally conservative in quant aggressiveness — default profiles prefer batching + cache over aggressive quantization unless safe-probe metrics show minimal quality/latency regressions.
